description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for grids/latlon3d/rules/ppm_D_lon_periodic (Piecewise Parabolic Method, Colella-Woodward 1984, semi-discrete method-of-lines flux) driven by problems/latlon3d_advection_zonal_ppm.esm — the rank-3 zonal analogue of advection_1d_ppm_periodic with passive lat (NLAT=5) and lev (NLEV=4) axes. The problem is loaded once per resolution with the loader-API metaparameter binding (esm-spec 9.7.6 binding site 4): NLON is the open metaparameter; the problem's dlon_deg observed divides by the NLON name, so the geometry follows each rebinding automatically. Exact solution sin((pi/180)(lon - omega t)) cos((pi/180) lat), independent of lev. HONEST ORDER: PPM is nominally 3rd order (parabolic reconstruction) and the UNLIMITED flux-difference is exactly the 4th-order central first derivative, but the original 1984 monotonicity limiter clips the two smooth extrema of the m=1 wave (the classic smooth-extremum clipping of the CW84 limiter, cured only by later extremum-preserving variants), flattening the parabola there. The global error is therefore dominated by a few isolated low-order points, giving a sub-nominal, norm-dependent observed order matching the 1-D cartesian sibling advection_1d_ppm_periodic almost exactly: the Julia golden gives median observed order 1.64 in L2 (pairwise 1.74, 1.64, 1.60) and 1.29 in Linf (pairwise 1.36, 1.29, 1.24). expected_order 1.45 with order_tolerance 0.25 brackets BOTH norm medians honestly (deviation 0.19 in L2, 0.16 in Linf); this is NOT a claim of 3rd-order convergence, which the CW84 limiter forecloses on any smooth periodic profile whose extrema always trigger the clip. Conservation is exact and is gated separately by the problem's mean assertion. MONOTONICITY UPGRADE (2026-07-13) -- ORDER RESET: stencils/ppm_flux now builds its edges on the CW84 eq. (1.8) MONOTONIZED slopes (ppm_face_value_mono) instead of the raw eq. (1.7) slopes. The previous eq.(1.10)-only chain was NOT bounded: verified IN-PIPELINE on rules/ppm_D_periodic with sharp non-negative ICs (square / spike / sawtooth, N=32/64/128), it drove the tracer to -5.3e-2 and overshot to 1.053, while the upgraded chain holds it EXACTLY in [0, 1] (min 0.0, max 1.0) on every profile and resolution. Both limiters are load-bearing -- eq. (1.8) bounds the interpolated edge, eq. (1.10)'s extremum-flattening branch stops outflux from a local minimum -- and neither alone suffices. The observed order therefore changes, and this manifest's expected_order is reset from the new Julia golden. NEW ORDER (upgraded): L2 median 1.88 (pairwise 1.81, 1.88, 1.92), Linf median 1.55 (1.55, 1.93, 1.06) -- both IMPROVED over the old eq.(1.10)-only chain (1.64 / 1.29). expected_order 1.70 +/- 0.30 brackets both medians (deviation 0.18 in L2, 0.15 in Linf). The pairwise orders are not monotone; that is limiter-activation noise, not a bad golden -- the set of cells where the CW84 clip fires shifts with resolution, so a smooth-MMS order estimate for a LIMITED scheme is intrinsically ragged. The gate brackets both norm medians with enough tolerance to absorb it.
